text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Meeting between Prime Minister Netanyahu and U.S. President Clinton today will decide future of American peace initiative.
- Netanyahu cancels appearance at Reform Jewish conference in United States; Reform leaders: he's evasive.
- Oman refuses to grant entry visa to Israeli diplomat.
- Fear in Israel of attack during Netanyahu's visit to United States.
- Palestinian President Arafat: Netanyahu sticks to fanatic ideology.
- European Union will discuss new initiative: end of violence and acceleration of final status negotiations.
- Housing ministry estimates: apartment prices won't rise also in 1997.
- Strauss asks permission to buy control of Elite.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israel rejects EU intervention.
- One injured in Israel Aircraft Industries factory blaze.
- State prosecutor Arbel weighs whether to levy charges in Bar-On affair.
- A sexy voice helps catch a thief.
- Knesset Finance Committee calls for June deadline for central bank reform.
- Israel Military Industries in black for first time since 1991.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu to Clinton: We'll continue on Har Homa but won't start new settlements.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu-Clinton meeting in White House today.
